sentences.text: Challenging the judgment and award passed in LAC No.87/2010, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The claimant's land was acquired in terms of Section 4(1) notification under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 on 16.10.2003.
The land bearing Sy.Nos.220/2A, 220/2B measuring 1 acre 30 guntas of Jaliberi village, Taluk Mudhol, District Bagalkot was acquired for public purpose.
3. The Special Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/- per acre.
The claimant sought reference seeking enhancement.
The Reference Court enhanced the compensation and awarded Rs.1,80,000/- per acre.
The claimant is before this Court seeking further enhancement.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant would submit that the land is an irrigated land and NC: 2023:KHC-D:10222 Rs.1,80,000/- per acre is awarded by the Reference Court is not adequate and just compensation and he would further submit that in Halaki village, Taluk Mudhol similar lands were acquired on 25.02.2002 and this Court in an appeal filed by the land-loser in MFA No.25466/2011 disposed of on 09.07.2015 has awarded compensation of Rs.2,20,000/- per care.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would submit that there is no scope for enhancement of compensation and market value determined by the Reference Court is just and proper which is based on evidence.

He would further submit that in MFA No.25466/2011 the Court was dealing with valuation of the land in Halaki village whereas in this case the Court is deciding the market value of the land situated at Jaliberi village of Mudhol Taluk.
Hence, the valuation determined in MFA No.25466/2011 cannot be made applicable to this case.
This Court has perused the aforementioned judgment as well as the judgment and award passed by the Reference Court which are under challenge.
7. The judgment and award which are under challenge would reveal that the lands in question are agricultural lands where sugarcane is grown.
The record of right would reveal that the claimant has grown sugarcane in the aforementioned lands.

sentences.text: In MFA No.25466/2011, this Court was also dealing with compensation payable in respect of the land where the sugarcane was grown.
It is to be noticed that the land in question in MFA No.25466/2011 was the land in Halaki village, Taluk Mudhol.
In this case the land is situated in Jaliberi village, Taluk Mudhol.
What could be noticed is both the villages are from the same taluk.

Since in both the lands sugarcane is grown and both lands are from same Taluk, this Court is of the view that the market value determined in MFA No.25466/2011 can be applied to NC:
2023:KHC-D:10222 determine the market value of the lands in question in this appeal.

9. So applying the valuation fixed by this Court in MFA No.25466/2011, this Court is of the view that the appeal is to be allowed in part and compensation of Rs.2,20,000/- per acre is to be awarded in respect of the lands acquired.

10. In view of the above, following order is passed:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The judgment and award dated 15.03.2012 passed in LAC No.87/2010 on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Mudhol are modified fixing the compensation as Rs.2,20,000/-
per acre with all statutory benefits, proportionate cost.

NC: 2023:KHC-D:10222 (iii) It is also noticed that this Court vide order dated 24.08.2023 has allowed the application for condonation of delay by excluding interest for the delayed period of 2001 days.
Accordingly, the appellant is not entitled to interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period of 2001 days.
